sections.title: Shrub and flowers
sections.text: Tabernanthe iboga is an evergreen Central African understorey shrub reaching about 4 m, with white latex and opposite, entire leaves. Its small, cream flowers have reddish to violet markings in the corolla.

sections.title: Fruit and root chemistry
sections.text: The smooth berry is about 3–6 cm long, yellow to red when ripe, and contains many seeds in white pulp. The root bark contains several alkaloids, including ibogaine; this is a potent psychoactive material, not food.

sections.title: Safety
sections.text: Clinical and toxicological reports associate ibogaine exposure with QT-interval prolongation and potentially life-threatening arrhythmias. The plate's pale flowers and yellow-orange fruit agree with botanical descriptions; no preparation or dose is implied.
